help.sections.overview.title: Overview
help.sections.overview.subtitle: Quick intro & terminology
help.sections.overview.content:
🧭 Overview

EduPlay Studio (eduplay-studio) helps teachers create learning games, preview them, and embed them into PowerPoint.

📌 Terms
• Project: a lesson/game you create (questions, settings, assets).
• Game type: Classic Quiz / Millionaire / Fishing…
• Preview: quick test inside the app.
• Play: full-screen play mode.
• Export: produce an output to share or embed elsewhere.
🧩 Components
• EduPlay Studio: create and manage projects.
• Edubot: AI assistant to generate/edit questions.
• PowerPoint Add-in: insert EduPlay games into PowerPoint slides.
✅ When using the PowerPoint Add-in
• Install the add-in once in EduPlay Studio.
• If Windows asks for Administrator permission during install, accept it so the add-in reliably shows up in PowerPoint.
• Restart PowerPoint after installation so the Add-ins menu refreshes.
help.sections.create_project.title: Create Project
help.sections.create_project.subtitle: Create and manage game projects
help.sections.create_project.content:
📁 Create a Project

All games you create are called projects.

✅ Step 1 — Create
Home screen → click CREATE NEW
→ enter name & description
→ choose a game type
→ click Create & Edit
✏️ Step 2 — Edit questions
• Click + Add question
• Choose question type
• Fill question/options/explanations
• Attach images/audio if needed
• Use Import to import from DOCX/Excel
🎮 Step 3 — Preview
• Use Preview in the editor
• Use Play on the home screen for full-screen mode
• Save frequently
help.sections.edubot.title: Edubot (AI)
help.sections.edubot.subtitle: Auto-generate questions with AI
help.sections.edubot.content:
🤖 Edubot — AI Assistant

Edubot is built-in. Open the app and click the 💬 chat button.

✨ Quick use
1. Open a project
2. Click 💬 to open Edubot
3. Type a request (e.g. "Create 5 math questions about fractions")
4. Questions are added automatically
📎 From documents
• Attach DOCX / PDF / TXT
• Then ask: "Create questions from this document"
help.sections.powerpoint_addin.title: PowerPoint Add-in
help.sections.powerpoint_addin.subtitle: Embed games into PowerPoint slides
help.sections.powerpoint_addin.content:
📊 PowerPoint Add-in

This feature lets you insert EduPlay games into PowerPoint slides for classroom use.

✅ Installation
1. In EduPlay Studio → Settings → Add-in tab → click Install / Repair Add-in
2. If Windows asks for Administrator permission, accept it
3. Close PowerPoint (if running) and reopen it
4. In PowerPoint, find the EduPlay button/tab on the ribbon (it may be under Add-ins)
👩‍🏫 How to use
1. In PowerPoint, open the EduPlay Add-in
2. Select your project in EduPlay Studio
3. In the add-in, click Insert Game to insert the game into the slide
🎮 Playing on slides
• Mouse/keyboard interactions stay inside the game frame — it won't auto-advance slides while you're interacting.
• To change slides even while focused in the frame: press →/↓ for next and ←/↑ for previous.
• Or click outside the frame and use arrow keys normally.
🛠️ Can't find the EduPlay button?
• Go back to EduPlay Studio → Settings → Add-in → click Install / Repair Add-in again
• Close/reopen PowerPoint (Office may cache the ribbon)
• In PowerPoint: File → Options → Add-ins → Manage: COM Add-ins → Go… and make sure EduPlay is enabled
• If still missing: restart your PC and try again
help.sections.interface.title: Interface
help.sections.interface.subtitle: Home, toolbar and navigation
help.sections.interface.content:
🖥️ Interface

EduPlay Studio is built around a simple home screen and a left toolbar.

🏠 Home screen
• Create: start a new learning project.
• Edit: open and continue a project you saved before.
• Play: test or publish the game you created.
⬅️ Left toolbar
Hover near the left edge of the window to open the toolbar.
It contains quick links to Home, Projects, Preview and Quick Actions.
🔧 Top-right buttons
• ? opens this help guide.
• ⚙ opens Settings (language, theme, AI, add-in).
The 💬 button in the bottom-right corner opens Edubot.
help.sections.preview_export.title: Preview & Export
help.sections.preview_export.subtitle: Test and share your game
help.sections.preview_export.content:
🚀 Preview & Export

Test your game inside EduPlay Studio, then share it with students.

👁️ Preview
• In the editor, use Preview to see how the game looks while you edit.
• From the left toolbar, open Preview to test the current project.
• From the home screen, Play runs the game full-screen.
📤 Export modes
When exporting, choose the mode that fits your class:
• Student mode: one attempt, final score is shown at the end.
• Teaching mode: retry allowed, answers can be revealed — great for live explanation.
🌐 Share your game
• Single-file HTML: one file you can send or upload.
• Firebase Hosting: publish online and share a link.
• PowerPoint Add-in: insert the game directly into a slide.
help.content:
NOTE: All games you create are called projects.

1) OVERVIEW / CREATE PROJECT (MANUAL)
- On the Home screen:
  - NEW: create a new project
  - EDIT: open and edit an existing project
  - PLAY: preview / view results
- Create a new project:
  1. Click NEW
  2. Enter name and description
  3. Choose game type (Classic Quiz / Who Wants to Be a Millionaire / Fishing)
  4. Click Create & Edit
- In the editor:
  - Add questions, answers, images/audio
  - Save often

2) EDIT WITH AI (EDUBOT)
- Before using AI: configure GROQ_API_KEY (or EDUPLAY_GROQ_API_KEY).
- Open Edubot via the floating chat button.
- Example prompts:
  - Create 10 grade-3 math questions about multiplication
  - Rewrite 5 questions to be easier to understand
  - Generate answers and short explanations
- After AI generates questions: drag/drop or add to the project and refine if needed.

3) INSTALL ADD-IN & INSERT GAME INTO POWERPOINT
- Install add-in:
  1. Open EduPlay Studio → Settings → Add-in → Install / Repair Add-in
  2. Accept Admin permission (if prompted)
  3. Close and reopen PowerPoint
  4. Open the EduPlay Add-in in PowerPoint
- Insert game into PPT:
  1. In EduPlay Studio: export the game as single-file HTML
  2. In PowerPoint: open the EduPlay Add-in
  3. In the add-in: select HTML file → import/insert → save into the PPT
  4. If needed: insert a placeholder to show the embedded viewer on the slide
- When playing in the slide viewer:
  - Mouse/keyboard focus stays inside the game frame and won't auto-advance slides
  - Press →/↓ for next slide, ←/↑ for previous slide
  - Or click outside the frame and change slides normally

credits.title: Credits
credits.ack.title: Acknowledgements
credits.ack.body:
EduPlay Studio sincerely expresses its gratitude to the individuals, communities, and organizations whose work, ideas, and contributions have directly or indirectly supported the development of this project.

We would like to thank:
• Kenney (Kenney Vleugels) for providing high-quality, free game assets that greatly support educational and indie game development.
• Sefton Kimberley Downes for the Who Wants to Be a Millionaire (WWBM) project, which served as a valuable technical and conceptual reference in the study of quiz-based game mechanics.
• The open-source community for sharing knowledge, tools, and resources that make learning and software development more accessible to everyone.

We also acknowledge the authors, researchers, and designers whose work has shaped the educational and design philosophy behind EduPlay Studio, including:
• James Paul Gee
• Karl Kapp
• Contributors to Bloom’s Taxonomy
• Don Norman

Additionally, we appreciate the inspiration drawn from existing educational and creative platforms such as Scratch, Construct, GDevelop, Wordwall, Kahoot, and Quizizz, which demonstrate effective ways to simplify complex processes for learners.

This project was developed for educational purposes, with respect for intellectual property and a commitment to ethical learning and software development.
